title: The knowledge graph — #277 audit, the decisions (v2)
headline: Six decisions about the shape of the designer brain — and what the agent reads when it builds.

decisions.title: The layers — five ingestion waves, or three views by force? One letter, then one word.
decisions.lede: The five layers as built are the order the graph was landed in: base wiring, rulings, the WCAG corpus, the {rules_total} HSBC rules, the {ux_total} UX principles — each behind the chip its lane earned. They are not five kinds of knowledge. The proof is accessibility: it sits in three of the five today — {a11y_sc} WCAG criteria in “guidelines”, {a11y_rules} rules from the accessibility-*.md files in “guideline rules”, {a11y_ux} standards-family principles in “UX principles” — with {a11y_links} edges between the three holdings (s275-D4 said so and deferred the joins to a named lane). The record called “governance” is measured, by the extractor’s own gov_target() test, as {rul_system} of {rul_total} rulings that govern only files, scripts and notes, {rul_design} that govern only components, {rul_both} both — a proxy from governs[] targets, not a reading of each ruling: about three-quarters of the record is how the system was built, one quarter is design precedent. This card asks two things and only two: a letter for the views, and a word for the name of the record.
options: a

One graph, three views by force. System (what exists — the agent chooses here) · Design governance (what a design must or should do — the agent obeys here) · Explanation (why — the agent consults here). The WCAG criteria, the accessibility rules and the design-scoped rulings are shown as one obligation with three provenances as sub-chips. Storage untouched: no node id, no edge type, no file under knowledge/ changes — the template’s chips and the fam labels do. Refines s275-D6 (“behind its own chip” — a sub-chip is still its own chip). It is not the lane s275-D4 deferred the 20 standards-family joins to: those are new authored edges of a new type and are priced separately in Part E (G3).
b

Keep the five, relabel. The chips stay as landed; only the word on the governance chip changes to whatever you pick below. Cheapest; leaves accessibility in three places and leaves the reader (D-3), when it exists, to assemble “what must this do” from four stores.
c
One graph, no views. Drop the chips; every kind is one colour on one canvas. Loses what s275-D6 wanted visible and gives the reader no precedence order either.

word.label: The name of the ruling record — one word
word.hint: Codex · Constitution · System management · or your own word. The record is the {rul_total} rulings with their evidence and sessions; it is not one of the three views.

decisions.why: Option (a), and the word is yours. Your instinct is right about the symptom: the categorisation is the commit history, and accessibility does belong in design governance. The cut by force (chooses / obeys / consults) is lane A2’s preference argued in prose — any re-cut fixes the measured symptom; this one gives the reader (D-3) a single verb per view. Force is a property of the edge, not the node: an obeys, appliesTo or design-scoped governs edge is an obligation wherever it lands. That is how the view handles the one leak A2V found — the {obeys_ux_edges} obeys→ux: edges s276-D3 ratified ({obeys_ux_metas} metas citing {obeys_ux_laws} of the six A-grade laws with a $why): the edge is drawn in Design governance, the principle node stays in Explanation, and no edge is renamed. Not asked on this card, and unratified — lane A2’s proposal for you to author or refuse later: (i) a precedence ladder (law, then ruling, then BLOCKING, then ADVISORY, then the principles) — nothing in _rulings.json orders a ruling against a WCAG criterion today, and s277-D3 left the one known conflict open; (ii) a derived scope on every ruling from its governs[] targets ({rul_system}/{rul_design}/{rul_both}), which over-counts as “system” the rulings that shape the designer brain (s269-D3, s274-D12, s275-D4); (iii) the dozen fences written once as a document — four are named today (fence 3 of #261, the two-red law, nam-002, “an instrument without a consumer is refused”), the rest are not. What the agent does differently under (a): nothing until D-3 wires a reader — then the reader asks one question per view instead of learning four stores and {a1_edge_types} edge types.
decisions.attrib: Lane A2 (Fable) proposed; lane A2V (Fable) counter-argued and split the card; lane A2F rewrote it on A2V’s verdict. Figures re-driven by A2V from the extractor’s own gov_target().

decisions.title: How do the {rules_total} HSBC rules reach a component?
decisions.lede: Today a rule reaches a component only by an edge to that component: obeys on {comp_with_obeys} metas, {rules_obeyed} rules, {files_reached} of {rules_files} guideline files — the {files_named} named after a component (s276-D5) plus the data-visualisation family file (s277-D3). The other {files_unreached} files hold {rules_unreached} rules that bind a facet every component has: copywriting {f_copy}, tone of voice {f_tone}, colour {f_colour}, typography {f_type}, icons and pictograms {f_icons}, neurodiversity {f_neuro} — {a11y_rules} of the {rules_unreached} are accessibility rules, and {cites_edges} of those already cite an SC that names components, so they are not facet rules. A designer knows the tone-of-voice rules apply to every label on the screen. The graph cannot say so, which is why {blocking_unbound} of the {blocking} BLOCKING rules bind nothing from the agent’s seat ({blocking_via_cites} of the {blocking_unbound} reach a component in two hops through cites → appliesTo; {blocking_unbound_any} reach nothing by any path). s277-D3 priced the per-component route for one family file and refused the all-to-all shape; the family-node option was declined because nothing could carry it.
options: a

A scope per guideline file. {rules_files} rows, authored once by a lane and read by Dave: universal (copy, tone, neurodiversity), facet:<token group> (colour → rag/ background/ …, type → text/ font-, icons → icon/), or component:<slug> (the {files_reached} already reached). Applicability then derives structurally through the tokens block {metas_tokens} metas already carry — no regex, no sentence per pair. obeys stays for the specific binding; an exception row per file (obeysNot) is the declared escape. Cost: {rules_files} rows, one reader of about forty lines, one lane. Consistent with s274-D9 (an attribute, not a hub). It is inference by declared scope — honest inference, labelled derived, never authored — and s277-D3’s own measurement is the precision evidence: 3 of 19 family rules did not bind all three charts, so expect exceptions at the same rate.
b

Continue the per-meta obeys route. The s276-D3 / s277-D1..D3 shape, file by file: about ten metas a lane, one sentence a pair. It reaches the component-named files and stops there — the {rules_unreached} facet rules would need {metas_total} × {rules_unreached} sentences (the all-to-all bound) to say what one attribute says.
c

A family or facet node with an inheritance edge. s277-D3 option (c): a new node kind, a new edge type and a propagation rule — three vocabulary changes — to carry what a {rules_files}-row attribute carries.
decisions.why: Option (a). It is the single change that moves the most obligations into the agent’s reach for the least authored work, and it is the s274-D9 shape (one place for one fact) rather than the s274-D12 shape (inference wearing a ref) — provided the derived binding is labelled derived and carries its exception row. The join key it needs — which token groups a component uses — is already a typed field in the metas and is what D-5 turns into nodes. For the thin slice (Part A) this is the leg that changes most: today _compose_slice.py attaches BLOCKING rules by a hand-written vocabulary dictionary and marks them “routed”; under (a) the same attachment is a structural join and the label becomes “derived”.
decisions.attrib: Lane A2 (Fable); the BLOCKING count is measured over _rules-index.json against every meta’s edges.obeys; the two-hop and named-file counts are lane A2V’s.

decisions.title: The thin slice at build time — wire the reader, or keep reading the metas?
decisions.lede: {a1_nc_types} edge types carrying {a1_nc_edges_fmt} live edges — {a1_nc_pct}% of the graph — are read by nothing, and {a1_schema_only} more are permitted by the schema and read by nothing. Not because they are wrong: {nc_answering_word} of the twelve (evidencedBy, appliesTo, ruledIn, definedIn) answer a designer’s question directly. Because the reader they were built for does not exist. The generate skill’s step 1 reads showroom/index.json ({showroom_index_k}K tokens) and then the metas it names — the library is {metas_total_all} files, about {metas_tokens_k}K tokens ({metas_mb} MB) — and names three edge types in total; the pack ships _rulings.json empty by design and does not ship the rule nodes or the principle nodes. One tool already does the right thing: knowledge/_compose_slice.py turns a task sentence into roles → components → edges → BLOCKING rules → anti-neighbours → token groups → rulings at {slice_dash_k}K tokens against {slice_dash_metas_k}K for the {slice_dash_metas} metas it replaces on a dashboard task ({slice_dash_ratio}×; {slice_bar_ratio}× on a four-meta bar-chart task; {slice_form_ratio}× on a fourteen-meta form) — and it is marked PROPOSAL, ADVISORY, NOT WIRED, with the wiring recorded as yours to rule. Part A below is the thin slice in full: what is read today, what the slice reads, what each decision on this page does to it, and the contract.
options: a

Wire it, under the thin-slice contract. _compose_slice.py becomes the generate skill’s step 1 at the next pack cut, with the contract in Part A: in — intent, data shape, roles and an optional component set, plus a token budget; out — the components chosen and why, the obligations (design rulings by id and date, rules by id with destiny and whether the binding is authored or derived), the must-nots (including the declared nulls with their $note), the token groups with tier, the assets, and what it could not resolve — sized to the budget, every row naming the edge that put it there. Extended to read the rule and principle stores by view (D-1), the file scopes (D-2) and the token nodes (D-5). Every consumer-less edge type gets its consumer in one move; s274-D11’s principle — an instrument without a consumer is refused, the reader lands in the same commit — finally applies to the graph itself. Cost: one lane on the slice, one pack cut; touches the pack-manifest rulings (s269-D9 pins _search_core.py, so the slice ships beside it, not inside it).
b

Keep read-the-metas. The graph stays a human’s explorer; the {a1_nc_types} types stay explorer-only; the agent’s design-time answer rate stays at {q_design}/12 whatever D-1, D-2 and D-5 land, and step 1 stays a judgement call about which of {metas_total_all} files to open.
c
Retire the {a1_nc_types} consumer-less types. Makes the census clean by deleting the answers to Q1, Q2, Q5, Q6 and Q11 before anyone has asked them.
decisions.why: Option (a). Every other decision on this page changes what the agent does only after this one; it is the decision, and the thin slice is its instrument. The answer rate the audit measures — {q_answered} of 12 by graph path, {q_design} of 12 reachable at design time — is the gap between a graph that exists and a graph that is consulted. A3’s ASK door (D-6 a) is this same lane by another name: one instrument, two verbs — compose a screen, ask one question.
decisions.attrib: Lane A2 (Fable), on the consumer census in A1 §4 and the compose-path read in its §6; the slice re-run on three tasks and the step-1 figures are lane A2F’s (slice-measure-v2.json); the 415K and the “four” are lane A2V’s corrections.

decisions.title: The vocabulary — {a1_edge_types} storage types, and what the agent is told
decisions.lede: A1 finds the real concentrations: thirteen component→component types and eleven ruling→ruling types. Both were ratified deliberately — s267-D3 retyped twenty ruling edges by hand into those eleven. The conductor’s suspected cluster (governs / boundBy / enforcedBy / under / appliesTo) is six different endpoint signatures, not one. The only true inverse pair is governs ({governs_n}) / governedBy ({governedBy_n}), and that is two ends of one authored join, not a synonym. The {a1_edge_types} types cost the system a line each in the validator and the explorer; they cost the agent nothing, because the agent is told three.
options: a

A reading vocabulary, storage untouched. Twelve verbs the agent will ever be told — is-a · contains · sits-with · must-not-sit-with · yields-to · renders-as · lives-in · provides/answers · must · should · rests-on · decided — mapped onto the {a1_edge_types} storage types in one table the reader (D-3) and the skills use. must is appliesTo, obeys→BLOCKING and the design-scoped governs; rests-on is obeys→ux: — which is how D-1’s force-of-the-edge reading is written down. definedIn, enforcedBy, flaggedBy, checkedBy, verifiedBy, boundBy, enClause, under, cites, mentions are machinery the reader uses and the agent never names. Touches no ruling.
b
Merge in storage. Fold the eleven ruling verbs and the thirteen component verbs into fewer types. Touches s267-D3, s270-D2, s274-D8, s275-D2 and s276-D3 by name, to save nothing the agent pays for.
c
Leave it. Fifty-one types, three named to the agent, and every new lane adds its own.
decisions.why: Option (a). The cost of {a1_edge_types} types is in the reader, not in the agent; a merge undoes a hand-ratified set to tidy a census. The prose tier stays as it is — mentions dashed and advisory under s267-D3, cites kept solid but labelled “parsed citation” because the author wrote the SC number in the rule text. For the thin slice this changes the labels on the output, not its content: the slice’s sections become the twelve verbs.
decisions.attrib: Lane A2 (Fable), on A1 §4’s endpoint signatures and §5’s join classes.

decisions.title: Tokens enter the graph — at what grain, and when?
decisions.lede: There is no token: node, so Q9 — what tokens does this component consume and what breaks if I change one — cannot be asked of the graph. Yet tokens is a typed block in {metas_tokens} of {metas_total} metas ({token_refs} distinct references across {token_groups} groups; the top twelve — text/, rag/, tertiary/, form/, border-radius/, icon/ … — carry {token_top12_pct}% of the {token_mentions} group-mentions; {token_files} live token files), and tokens/_blast-radius.json already computes reach — so an honest today-cost for Q9 is about {q9_today_k}K tokens (the meta plus the blast-radius file), not the {q9_a3_k}K A3 charged by reading canon.css. s269-D3 ruled the grain — its ruled text, verbatim: “TOKENS ENTER THE GRAPH AT TIER GRAIN - semantic versus primitive - and NEVER as 932 leaf nodes.” Nothing was built. D-2’s facet scopes key on exactly these groups.
options: a

Group grain with its tier, now — as _compose_slice.py already reads it. The token group (text, rag, form … about {token_groups} of them, the top twelve carrying {token_top12_pct}% of references) as the token: node, each carrying its tier (semantic · component-type · foundation · primitive) as an attribute; bindsToken minted structurally from each meta’s tokens block; blast radius carried from _blast-radius.json as an attribute. Roughly a hundred nodes and a thousand edges, one lane, no sentence authored. The ruling’s word is tier; group-with-tier is how the repo has operationalised it since #269 (_compose_slice.py: “a slice names the token GROUP and its tier, never the leaves”). The P-269-7 tripwire is met by building the thing it waits for.
b
Wait for the tripwire. P-269-7 fires when _GRAPH-REPORT.md next regenerates. D-2 then has no structural join key and falls back to naming token groups by hand in each scope row.
c

Leaf grain. 932 nodes by the ruling’s count ({token_leaves_live} in the ten live files today; 1,043 in _blast-radius.json). Refused by s269-D3 as a graph that cannot be read; listed so the refusal is visible — and so that A3’s TOKENS shape (D-6 d, about 950 nodes) is seen for what it is: this option, whatever its tier is called.
decisions.why: Option (a). It is the cheapest structural family left — a typed field in {metas_tokens} metas that nobody has turned into edges — and it is the join key D-2 uses, so the two land together or D-2 lands weaker. For the thin slice it changes the source of the tokens leg, not its output: today tokens_for() regexes the group out of each meta’s token strings and looks the tier up in a map built from eight files at load; under (a) it walks bindsToken and reads the tier off the node.
decisions.attrib: Lane A2 (Fable); the group census is its measurement (A2-measure.json §tokens). The s269-D3 wording, the 792 live leaves, the ≈25K Q9 cost and the group-with-tier reading are lane A2V’s call (VERIFY.md Part 2, D-5).
